title: Georgian Lobio with Skillet Mchadi Corn Cakes
dek: Creamy, partly crushed red kidney beans get their depth from browned onion, garlic, coriander, fenugreek, walnuts, herbs and vinegar, with crisp-edged white-cornmeal mchadi made while the beans simmer.
image_alt: Thick herb-flecked red bean lobio in one handled clay cup beside a golden round mchadi corn cake resting over a second clay cup
ingredients: 1 lb dried red kidney beans, sorted and rinsed
Water for soaking, plus 10 cups fresh water for cooking
2 1/2 tsp Diamond Crystal kosher salt, divided, plus more to taste
1 tsp ground blue fenugreek or 3/4 tsp regular ground fenugreek
3 tbsp sunflower oil or other neutral oil, divided
1 large yellow onion, cut into 1/4-inch dice
1 tsp dried summer savory or dried thyme
2 tbsp red wine vinegar, plus more to taste
1 packed cup cilantro leaves and tender stems, finely chopped, divided
2 cups fine white cornmeal, preferably stone-ground (not cornstarch)
1 tbsp sunflower oil, for the skillet

instructions.name: Soak the kidney beans for at least five hours
instructions.text: Put the sorted beans in a large bowl and cover with cool water by at least 3 inches. Soak for 5 to 12 hours; the five-hour minimum follows current FDA guidance for red kidney beans. Drain in a colander, discard the soaking water and rinse the beans well. Do not use a slow cooker for the raw beans.

instructions.name: Give the beans a full safety boil
instructions.text: Transfer the soaked beans to a 6-quart Dutch oven with 10 cups fresh water and the bay leaves. Bring to a vigorous rolling boil over high heat and boil uncovered for 30 full minutes, stirring twice and adding a little boiling water if needed to keep the beans submerged. A low simmer is not a substitute for this initial boil because properly cooking red kidney beans is what destroys their natural lectin.

instructions.name: Simmer until the centers are completely creamy
instructions.text: After the 30-minute boil, reduce the heat to maintain a steady simmer. Stir in 1 teaspoon salt and cook partially covered for 35 to 60 minutes, stirring every 15 minutes, until several beans from different parts of the pot mash smoothly with no chalky core. Keep the beans covered by about 1 inch of liquid, adding boiling water as necessary. Reserve 2 cups cooking liquid, then drain the beans and discard the bay leaves.

instructions.name: Toast and grind the walnut-spice seasoning
instructions.text: While the beans simmer, toast the walnuts in a dry 12-inch skillet over medium heat for 4 to 6 minutes, tossing often, until fragrant; transfer to a plate. Toast the coriander seeds in the same skillet for about 60 seconds. Cool 5 minutes, then pulse the walnuts, coriander, fenugreek, red pepper flakes, 1/2 teaspoon salt and 2 grated garlic cloves in a food processor until finely pebbly but not oily. Set aside and wipe the skillet clean.

instructions.name: Brown the onion and bloom the aromatics
instructions.text: Heat 2 tablespoons sunflower oil in the Dutch oven over medium. Add the diced onion and 1/2 teaspoon salt; cook 8 to 10 minutes, stirring, until soft and golden at the edges. Add the remaining 3 grated garlic cloves and the summer savory and stir for 30 seconds, just until fragrant.

instructions.name: Crush the beans into a thick, spoonable lobio
instructions.text: Add the drained beans and 1 1/4 cups reserved cooking liquid to the onions. Mash about two-thirds of the beans with a potato masher, leaving whole beans visible. Stir in the walnut-spice mixture and simmer gently for 10 to 15 minutes, stirring and scraping the bottom often, until thick enough to mound on a spoon but still loose enough to settle in a bowl. Add reserved liquid 1/4 cup at a time if it tightens too far.

instructions.name: Season the finished lobio for balance
instructions.text: Stir the red wine vinegar, three-quarters of the cilantro, the scallions and the remaining 1/2 teaspoon salt into the lobio. Simmer 2 minutes, then remove from the heat and rest covered for 10 minutes. Taste and add more salt or vinegar in small increments; the beans should be savory, gently tart and aromatic rather than aggressively sour.

instructions.name: Mix and shape six mchadi corn cakes
instructions.text: While the lobio rests, combine the white cornmeal and remaining 1/2 teaspoon salt in a bowl. Stir in 1 1/3 cups hot tap water. When cool enough to handle, knead in the bowl for 1 minute, adding the remaining water 1 tablespoon at a time until the mixture holds together when squeezed without oozing. With damp hands, shape 6 compact patties about 3 1/2 inches wide and 1/2 inch thick, smoothing any cracked edges.

instructions.name: Cook the mchadi until crisp and cooked through
instructions.text: Heat the clean 12-inch skillet over medium and add 1 tablespoon sunflower oil. Arrange the mchadi in one layer and cook for 6 to 8 minutes per side, adjusting the heat so they become deeply golden without scorching. Stand each cake on its edge with tongs for about 30 seconds where needed. The centers should feel firm rather than wet or gritty; transfer to a rack and rest 5 minutes.

instructions.name: Serve the two photographed components hot
instructions.text: If the rested lobio is stiffer than a thick stew, loosen it with a splash of reserved cooking liquid and rewarm to a simmer. Spoon into six warm bowls or handled cups, leaving the partly crushed texture visible, and finish with the remaining cilantro. Serve one round golden mchadi alongside or perched over each cup, matching the photographed presentation.

why_it_works: A five-hour soak, discarded soak water and a full 30-minute boil in fresh water follow FDA guidance for reducing the phytohaemagglutinin naturally concentrated in red kidney beans.
Mashing only part of the beans releases enough starch for a cohesive, creamy stew while retaining the whole-bean texture visible in the finished lobio.
Toasted walnuts thicken and enrich the beans without dairy, while coriander, fenugreek, summer savory, garlic and cilantro build layered aroma at different stages.
Vinegar goes in after the beans are fully tender, so acidity brightens the rich walnut mixture without slowing the softening of the bean skins.
Hot water hydrates fine cornmeal quickly, and compact patties cooked over moderate heat develop golden crusts before their centers dry out.
swaps: For a faster version, replace the dried beans with four 15-ounce cans red kidney beans, drained and rinsed. Skip the soak and safety-boil steps; simmer the canned beans with 2 cups low-sodium vegetable broth for 15 minutes before mashing.
If blue fenugreek is unavailable, use 3/4 teaspoon regular ground fenugreek. It is stronger and more bitter, so do not substitute it measure for measure.
Dried summer savory best matches the bean-friendly herbal profile, but dried thyme works at the same quantity and is easier to find.
Use yellow cornmeal if fine white cornmeal is unavailable. The mchadi will taste similar but will not have the pale golden color shown in the photograph.
For a nut-free lobio, omit the walnuts and pulse 1/2 cup toasted sunflower seeds with the spices. This is a practical adaptation, not a claim that the flavor is identical.
storage: Cool lobio in shallow containers within 2 hours and refrigerate at 40°F or below for up to 4 days. Refrigerate mchadi separately in an airtight container for up to 3 days. Reheat lobio in a saucepan with a splash of water, stirring frequently, until it reaches 165°F and bubbles throughout; reheat mchadi on a dry skillet over medium-low for 2 to 3 minutes per side or in a 350°F oven for 8 to 10 minutes. Freeze lobio without the fresh finishing cilantro for up to 3 months, thaw overnight in the refrigerator and add fresh herbs after reheating. Mchadi is best fresh and can become crumbly after freezing.
notes: Current FDA natural-toxin guidance says to soak red kidney beans for at least 5 hours, discard that water and boil the beans in fresh water for at least 30 minutes. This recipe deliberately uses that more conservative current guidance and does not permit a slow cooker for raw kidney beans.

The 445-minute total includes a five-hour soak, 35 minutes of hands-on preparation and 110 minutes of cooking. An overnight soak changes the schedule but not the active work; soaked beans vary, so tenderness rather than a fixed simmer time is the reliable endpoint.

The CC BY 3.0 photograph was inspected at full size twice. It clearly shows thick, herb-flecked bean lobio in a handled clay cup and a round golden mchadi corn cake over a second cup; the title, method, serving direction and alt text are limited to those verifiable components.

Mchadi is a Georgian cornmeal bread. This skillet version uses fine white cornmeal, water and salt, with a thin film of oil for dependable release on a home stove; it should be compact and crisp-edged, not fluffy like leavened cornbread.
Calories and cost estimate one-sixth of the bean-and-walnut mixture plus one mchadi. Prices vary by region, but dried beans, cornmeal and onion keep the core meal economical.

faqs.q: Can I cook the dried kidney beans for lobio in a slow cooker?
faqs.a: Not from raw. FDA guidance warns that low slow-cooker temperatures may not destroy kidney-bean lectin. Soak the beans at least 5 hours, discard the water and boil them vigorously in fresh water for 30 minutes as written before any gentler simmer. Canned kidney beans are already fully cooked and can be used for the faster variation.

faqs.q: Why are my beans still firm after the listed simmer time?
faqs.a: Older beans and hard water can take longer. Keep them submerged with boiling water and continue simmering until several beans mash without a chalky center; another 20 to 40 minutes is normal for stubborn beans. Do not add the vinegar until they are completely tender, because acid can slow softening.

faqs.q: How do I stop mchadi from cracking or staying raw in the middle?
faqs.a: Use fine cornmeal, add hot water gradually and squeeze the mixture before shaping: it should hold firmly without leaking water. Compress each patty and smooth cracks with damp fingers. Keep the cakes about 1/2 inch thick and cook over moderate, not high, heat for 6 to 8 minutes per side so the center hydrates before the crust darkens.
